the N-termini of synthetases are amphiphilic, and the basic amphiphilic character of the N-terminin of yeast synthetases is evolved to a neutral character in the mammalian synthetates.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the evolution and association of synthetase enzymes in eukaryotic organisms.
the structure-function relationship of synthetases with a special emphasis on the synthetase-synthetase interaction.
the structural basis of the synthetase multienzyme complexes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal region is the most variable part of the aminoacyl-tRNAsynthetases, and that the N-terminal helix of aspartyl-tRNAsynthetas is unique in its amphiphilic nature.

the N-terminal sequence of aspartyl-tRNAs synthetases has been evolving in an unusual way, with an increasing number of charged residues and a decreasing number of hydrophobic residues in mammalian synthetasses.
